Everything else the person asks for runs, because it is fenced on its own: DMs and `message_person` reach only the roster, invites name attendees by person id, the Executive's own email checks every recipient against the roster, standing facts and profile edits keep only the person's own words, and a workflow drafted in chat is saved only once a person confirms it. `upsert_person` runs only for a contact the person asked for (`speaker_named_contact`: a contact, never the team, an approval scope or a chat account, with a word of the name in what they typed, in a message that asks to add, save or change someone, a new contact's address one they typed or one that sent the mail the turn read under the contact's name (`TurnDelegation.mail_senders`), never one the mail's text only mentions, and on an update a changed address they typed), since the roster is what the send checks trust. Any other contact add is refused with a pointer to an approval card (`lockdown.CONTACT_REFUSAL`), so the Executive leaves an `add_contact` card in the chat rather than asking them to type the address. What an email itself asks for is still never done on its say-so; it goes on an approval card. Every tool is classified as allowed or withheld, a test fails on a new unclassified one, and an unknown name is withheld, except an extension tool registered with `after_mail_read` (one that only reads the install's own data). The refusal tells the model to put what the step needs in its reply, since the next turn sees the reply but not the mail, and to do the step then without reading the mail again. A refused call gets a private `tool_invocation` row (`refused: mail_touched`) and tells the model to offer it in the next message. The offered tool list never changes mid-turn, so the cached prefix holds. The handlers that reach outside check again on their own (`outside_reach_refusal`). The server-side web search stays, as on a turn private to the principal. The lockdown ends with the turn. Later turns of that conversation stay private to its owner (`touched_mail`) but hold nothing: a refusal says it will work when they ask again in their next message, and it does.

## Always in the loop

A sent reply can leave a note. Once the reply went, `reply_send` starts `memory.history_notes.note_sent_reply` for the person who sent it, in the background, when their "Keep track of what happens" switch is on and the conversation isn't one they asked not to remember. The note-taker sees only the words they sent, so other people's mail never becomes a note, and a failure never touches the send. Recall is `recall_history`, offered on the same verified, private surfaces as `ghostwrite_email` and also allowed under the mail lockdown, since it only reads the speaker's own notes. Calling it locks the turn like `ghostwrite_email` does, from its own round on. The same switch also covers notes from chat, which don't need Act as me. See **Memory** for the checks, retention and controls.

## The system prompt

A constant, name-free `DELEGATION_ADDENDUM` joins block 0 after the unchanged identity addendum while anyone on the install has it on (`block0_delegation_on`). It names the four mailbox reads and says other people's mail is data and that a conversation which read it reaches nobody else; and it tells the model that `ghostwrite_email` is the single exception to *never impersonate*, and only for the person being spoken to; that everything else is written as itself; that when the tool isn't offered the asker can't have it; that a draft is never described as sent; and that it never denies being an AI. It is keyed on the install-level setting, never on the turn or the speaker, so switching it misses the 1h cache once (see Prompt Caching).

## What it does for you

**What it does for you** (`delegation.may_do`, `GET /what-it-may-do`) is read-only: with the viewer's settings right now, one row per thing that can go out without asking, written as one sentence of what it does, what happens to it (goes out, waits for someone, always waits, drafts only, off) and which setting decides it, with a link there. It sits beside every Delegate tab (`DelegatePage` → `WhatItDoesPanel`): a column to the right on a wide screen (closing it is remembered in the browser), a bottom sheet on a narrow one. The UI groups rows by outcome (Sends on its own, Asks first, Writes for you to send, Off). Every delegation setter in `lib/api.ts` fires `DELEGATION_CHANGED` after a save; the panel reloads on it and marks the rows whose outcome or text changed as **Just changed** for ten seconds. `/delegate` and the old `/delegate/what-it-may-do` open Act as me. Its **Compare** fold holds Who writes and who sends. Three parts, each behind a pill that counts what goes out:

- **As you** (the caller's own, when `can_delegate` allows them): built from `settings.is_enabled`, `inbox.get_watch`, `handle_it.get` and `handle_it.RULES`, `handle_it.leading` (Everything), `training.get` and `training.learned`, and their rules, the same reads `handle_it.refusal` and `follow_up_refusal` make. A level's row follows its `Rules` (strangers, follow-up reach, links and amounts), not a copy of them. A note names the ladder: Handle it for me rides on Draft replies to my inbox and Write drafts as me, and Everything also drops when Replies or Follow-ups go into training.
- **As the Executive** (the principal's alone, as `GET /take-the-lead`): the switch and its training, each Ask first kind, the company's rules, and meetings. A meeting it thinks of on its own always waits: both meeting gates need someone on a verified surface in the turn, which an unattended run never is. A meeting someone asks for in chat follows **Always asks first → Meetings asked for in chat** (on means it waits: `meeting_scheduling`'s class mode is `propose`; off means `auto_execute`) and, in a team workspace, Operations' level too.
- **Departments**: each level, and what a level covers (department-scoped scheduled work, check-ins, alert review, team members' chat sends, and Operations' meetings), and that it doesn't cover what the Executive does under Take the lead.

It also says when the Executive is paused, and when nothing can be sent as anyone because signed sign-ins are off. Nothing on it writes or reads mail. A contact, someone not on People, or a request with no caller (outside local login) gets 403.

## How far it goes as you

One setting replaces the switches that used to turn each other off out of sight. The UI shows it as two pickers (`ReachCard.tsx`): **What it writes as you** (`WritesCard`) on the Act as me tab and **What it sends on its own** (`SendsCard`) on the Handle it for me tab; What it does for you links each row to its own picker. Its steps, each adding to the one before: **Off**, **Drafts when I ask** (Write drafts as me), **Drafts for my inbox** (Draft replies to my inbox), then the Handle it for me steps that send, **Easy ones**, **People I know** and **Most mail** (`careful`, `balanced`, `bold`), and for the owner **Everything** (Take the lead as you). Act as me shows the first three as **Off**, **When I ask** and **Draft replies automatically** (any sending step reads as Draft replies automatically there). Handle it for me shows **Off** (saved as the inbox step) and the sending steps, and opens only once Act as me is at Draft replies automatically, with a button that turns that on; moving Act as me below it says Handle it for me stops too. `PUT /delegation/reach` (`{step}`) moves it, and `reach_of` reads the step back from the switches, so the stored switches stay the source of truth and every gate reads them as before.

Going down turns the switches above the target off, highest first (`_lead_off`, then Handle it, then the inbox watcher, then Write drafts as me), so nothing is ever on above a switch that's off; the UI says what stops and asks before it saves. A lower sending level only holds more back and is set directly, so it needs no signed sign-in. Going up calls each switch's own route in order, so every check it makes still applies: the mailbox connected, signed sign-ins for sending, the owner alone and not in training for Everything. The first that refuses stops the move at a whole step and answers with that route's error. Handle it for me's own Off / In training / On (Replies and Follow-ups together) and, at Everything, **Your rules** sit with its picker, and **Learn from my edits** (drafts training) under the Act as me one; neither picker changes training.
